purpose: The prepared local layer lifecycle, replayed. Each case carries the op (without the schema wrapper) and the answer the kernel must give: the parsed answer, or {"error": "<the exact Err string>"} when the request itself is malformed. ds-web replays the same file through the vendored WASM and the native store replays it over a real catalogue file, so no rule here can be true on one host and not another.
source: Transcribed from ds-web src/lib/stores/sketches.ts (normalizeSourceMetadata, normalizedSourceKind, defaultSourceName, sketchLayerSourceLabel, normalizeFeatureStorage, normalizeMetaLayer, reconcileSourceOrigin, clampNumber, SKETCH_COLORS, createSketchLayer*, restoreSketches), 2026-09-11.
note: Re-record expected with DS_LOCAL_LAYERS_CASES_WRITE=1 cargo test --test local_layers_cases after a deliberate rule change, and say why in the commit.

cases.why: A drawn layer names only itself and its geometry; every other field of the descriptor — id, source name, source layer name, flat style, visibility, creation time — is the kernel's answer.
The colour comes from the shared SKETCH_COLORS palette at the index the host has reached, wrapping after ten, so a host never picks a colour.
A manual layer filed under its own name is filed under 'Manual layers' instead — the source label rule that kept the temporary layer panel from showing a folder per layer.
A folder connection is normalised: the file name is taken from the path and the format from the file name, both lower-cased, and a missing refresh time takes the host's clock.
An imported file keeps its container name, its inner member and its size; an empty source path and a non-positive timestamp are absent rather than zeroed.
Imported-file metadata belongs only to an import layer: a manual layer handed it has no source behind it, and half-kept provenance is never persisted.
A folder connection that cannot be reopened — no handle key — is not a folder connection, so the whole metadata is dropped rather than kept unusable.
Parked chunk storage is admitted with its render mode settled, its preview window clamped and its id prefix minted from the layer id — never from randomness.
A Project Work root is an ephemeral projection of canonical PM entities; admitting one as a persistent local layer would falsely imply the local copy is editable truth.

refusal.message: Project Work is an ephemeral governed map root, not a prepared local layer

cases.why: A feature count a host asserts is never negative; only restore repairs one, so a register that carries one is a malformed descriptor and nothing is admitted.

refusal.message: a feature count is never negative

cases.why: Every op names the scope it believes it is in; a catalogue from another store is never appended to.

refusal.message: the registry belongs to another local layer scope

cases.why: The same descriptor and the same answers under a native lane+uid scope: the browser profile is one store among others, not the shape of the rule.
A native catalogue is keyed by lane and uid: the same lane under another user is another store, and an op naming it changes nothing.

refusal.message: the registry belongs to another local layer scope

cases.why: A row persisted before ids were minted is reopened with one minted from the host's clock and its place in the store, and every defaulted field is named under repaired.
A style value out of range is clamped, not refused: the store must reopen. An unreadable number takes the default.
`visible !== false`: only a literal false hides a layer, so a row that never carried the field reopens visible.
The parity floor: rows the kernel itself admitted reopen identically, nothing is repaired and the host has nothing to rewrite.
A row that lost its colour takes the next palette entry, counted over the rows that needed one — the pure restatement of nextColor() at boot.
Project Work rows may not persist: they are retired rather than reopened, and the receipt names the payload record and parked chunks the host may delete for each.
A retired row’s parked chunks are released only when no reopened layer still parks its payload there; otherwise they are that layer’s storage and the receipt does not name them.
Two rows under one id cannot both be reopened and neither may be dropped silently, so the whole restore refuses and the host keeps its raw bytes.

refusal.message: local layer a appears twice in the store

cases.why: A retired Project Work row and a kept row with one id are one id twice: releasing the retired row’s payload would delete the kept layer’s, so the whole store refuses and the host keeps its raw bytes.

refusal.message: local layer sketch-1758000000000-1 appears twice in the store

cases.why: A folder connection missing its handle key is dropped and the drop is reported under repaired, so the host knows its persisted bytes are no longer the admitted store.
An unreadable column type reads as text and a nameless column is dropped; the user's columns survive a reopen.
A first run has nothing to reopen: a catalogue at revision zero, nothing retired, nothing to rewrite.
The reopen rules do not change with the store: a native lane+uid catalogue reopens exactly as the browser profile does.
A store whose rows are not descriptors is not a store; the kernel says so instead of inventing seventeen defaults.

refusal.message: record 0 of the local layer store is not an object

cases.why: A replaced payload always leaves the previously parked chunks behind; the receipt names them so the host can clear exactly that storage and nothing else.
Re-parking the same chunks is not a replacement: releasing them would delete the payload just written.
Storage a host offers must locate its chunks: an object the kernel cannot read is a malformed descriptor, refused whole, never a payload lost quietly while the previous chunks are released.

refusal.message: feature storage must name the upload chunks that hold the payload

cases.why: Chunks another layer of the catalogue still parks its payload in are that layer’s storage: replacing this layer’s payload releases nothing, so a release never names another layer’s record.
Connecting a layer to a folder is an admitted change of its origin, normalised by the same rule as at registration.
A null origin detaches the layer from its source; the layer itself stays.
A manual layer's name inside its source is its name, so a rename moves both; the name is trimmed and the source label is re-derived.
An imported layer keeps the name it had inside its file: renaming the map layer never rewrites its provenance.
A source is a label shared by layers: renaming it renames every layer of that kind under that label, and no layer under another.

The source label rule holds through a source rename: a manual layer whose own name is the new source name is filed under Manual layers, not under itself, so the admitted registry reopens without repair.
A style change inside the descriptor’s range is admitted as given and carries the rich style document untouched — the kernel never reads it.
Only restore clamps: a host asserting a style outside the descriptor’s range is refused whole, so nothing moves and no value is silently corrected.

refusal.message: a line width is 0.5 to 12

cases.why: Absent leaves the document alone, null clears it back to the flat colour and width.
What a visibility toggle writes to the map is layer_state's answer; that the catalogue remembers it is this module's.
An id the catalogue does not hold is a refusal, not an append.

cases.why: The proof that a removal cannot touch an original: the receipt names the layer's own payload record and its own parked chunks, never the source file it was imported from, its folder handle, another layer's storage or any project asset.
A layer whose features live in its own record releases exactly that record.
Removing a layer whose chunks another layer still parks its payload in releases only its own payload record: the chunks are the other layer’s storage and are never named.
Removing what is not there changes nothing and says so.

cases.why: A catalogue listing is bounded rows plus where each layer came from: never the style, never the schema, and never the folder handle key — a listing is not a capability.
The limit bounds the rows; the count is the catalogue, so a host knows there is more.
A catalogue with two layers under one id is not a catalogue; it is refused before anything is read from it.
